claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration from CDK to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, debugging was frustrating due to CloudFormation templates, and multi-cloud was nearly impossible.
SST was originally built on top of AWS CDK, which allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.

Comparison table: AWS CDK is AWS-only and supports only TypeScript and Python, while Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, on-prem and any programming language; Pulumi has faster deployment, real-time debugging; CDK uses CloudFormation state and AWS Secrets Manager only.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because of direct execution instead of CloudFormation.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets management.
CDK and CloudFormation act as a code generator producing an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises environments.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
Pulumi offers built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies 'day one' tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
Ion is the code name for a new SST deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine while also bridging Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make the underlying cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install, no Pulumi account and no Pulumi Cloud dependency; the Pulumi engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its deployment state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not in Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying full-stack applications to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file using SST components, and `sst deploy` handles provisioning.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built directly on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

The SST blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN)."

The SST blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources."
The SST docs ('What is SST') say: "SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi."

Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs, enabling resources with no SST constructs to be defined and deployed.

Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article 'SST ditches AWS CDK. Time to move on to Ion' says: "You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now."

SST's published platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls and @pulumiverse/vercel as direct dependencies, in the anomalyco/sst repository (formerly sst/sst).
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs. actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi/pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge was built specifically to let projects like SST reuse Terraform's provider ecosystem with the Pulumi engine.
The Pulumi engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
The provider bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.

Nitric runs application deployments through the Pulumi engine; its docs state "all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments", with official providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP and Azure providers.
Defang's pulumi-defang provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`; Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud.
SST constructs compile to Pulumi resources, so resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed in the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state; its Terraform providers are bridged through the Pulumi engine.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had about 796,000 (796,291) downloads for the week of September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode carries a larger GitHub star following than SST itself and has grown quickly since launch.
SST's release cadence and its dependency on the Pulumi engine have not changed as a result of the team's work on opencode.
Pulumi Cloud provides cross-team visibility into infrastructure state, policy as code provides guardrails enforced centrally, and components share infrastructure patterns across an organization.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code and components can be used with SST without leaving the Pulumi engine SST already uses.
SST does not expose cross-team visibility, policy enforcement, or infrastructure shared across more than one application on its own.
Nitric, Defang and SST expose a narrower, more opinionated interface while relying on the Pulumi engine and provider bridge underneath.
Embedding the Pulumi engine gives a framework a production-grade provisioning engine and hundreds of cloud providers.
